english_verification.review_scope: Read the opening history file; checked the English Ovdal Tûngr name and the Uthojdihr, Strongbellow Society, Steamers, and Sea Hold flavor strings. Read three supporting Markdown chunks from one fixed-revision Wiki page for the flooded-hold account, resettlement, maritime recovery, and blockade chronology. This was representative source checking, not a mission-tree audit. Primary compared all native idea names/descriptions by actual current English localisation key. Source ranges may be locator envelopes; conditional and predecessor idea sets remain separate. No formal validators, tests, builds or browser checks were run.
unresolved: Offline Wiki and historical sources differ on the exact ancient resettlement date; no single date is asserted.
Later alliance and blockade chronology, all Sea Hold upgrades, DLC combinations, and multiplayer outcomes were not exhaustively checked.
The local Mod's English country name is Ovdal Tûngr; the source's 2024/2025 multiplayer accounts do not pin a precise game version.

rationale.campaign_length: 38 dedicated mission definitions, including conditional continuations; the engineering arc can extend well into the late game.
rationale.colonization: Overseas routes reach Sarhal and Haless; the campaign is not simply about painting a continent.
rationale.complexity: Multiple unlock chains run alongside diplomacy, trade rights, advisors, Innovativeness, and capital requirements.
rationale.dark_story: Forced Goblin removal coexists with cross-cultural cooperation; maritime trade is not all portrayed as raiding.
rationale.difficulty: Pressure mainly comes from financial thresholds and preparation across several systems; no in-game difficulty test was performed.
rationale.diplomacy: An alliance or subject relationship with Crathánor, transferred trade rights, and cross-cultural cooperation affect progress.
rationale.early_pressure: Surface rivals and the early maritime economy require balancing army costs, fleets, and allies.
rationale.magic_artifice_intensity: Pumping, steam, ironclads, and a floating Sea Hold form the technological narrative.
rationale.narrative_density: The clan council, the Sea Gate Clan's influence, and Strongbellow engineering connect the country's transformation.
rationale.tall_play: The hold, shipyards, and development of the core province sustain a long tall-building campaign.
rationale.trade_economy: The navy, trade share, and overseas ports form the core wealth loop.
rationale.warfare: Taking land in Bahar, securing trade ports, and protecting routes require a fleet and some land warfare.

identity.appearance: A 1444 Copper Dwarf clan republic following Ancestor Worship, with its capital in province 526; Crathánor is a historic friend.
identity.formation_scope: Representative checks of missions, events, and unique decisions did not establish a Tag-changing successor; the Sea Hold is a maritime project of the same country, not a separate formable.
identity.region: Western Bulwar / the Bahar coast and Divenhal Sea

description.text: For millennia, Ovdal Tûngr lay hidden among the mountains, its lower levels flooded, its forges long gone cold. It was not rediscovered until 2181BA, during a survey ordered by Irsakar the Benevolent, God-King of Barzišah. Upon its discovery, Irsakar gifted the hold to the dwarves of his kingdom to resettle in exchange for their service. While most of the hold was inaccessible, the dwarves quickly went to work repairing the dry docks. Soon dwarven sailors would be found in every port across the Divenhal Sea.

description.text: With the reclamation of the hold, Irsakar declared that the dwarves would decide how to govern themselves. A council was convened of all the major clans in exile, including three remnants of the Serpentreach’s Noh-Kazaz, namely the Zonogherûd and Azgheledbul clans of Orlghelovar and the Aznezhyg clan of Lodhum. For decades, the council would convene and arguments would rage with each clan claiming legitimacy to rule the rest. In the interim, a single clan was selected with term limits of 20 years to administer the growing migration of petty dwarves from the Segbandal of the Middle Dwarovar. By 2064BA, with still no clan willing to give any other authority over the whole, it was decided that there would be no permanent ruling clan. Instead, elective governance would become law with its clan selected by the council. This was the origin of Tûngr’s Reachdwarf electorate clans ruling over a Segbandalic majority.

description.text: Most of the dwarves in Ovdal Tûngr are your typical stock, completely unaccustomed to seafaring. That is not true for the Uthojdihr, a clan that was founded after the reclamation. Referred to derogatively as the logr-drika (water-drinkers) by other dwarves, this clan is as much at home on the water as they are underground. While not all dwarven sailors belong to this clan, for much of history they were the most likely dwarves to be found trading hold supplies with Ruby Dwarves in Oldport, competing with the copper merchants of Busirat, haggling for grain along the Coast of Tears, or buying silks in Brasan. Throughout the ancient Divenhal, there was an Uthojdihr family in every port.

description.text: At the crossroads of Greater Castanor, Bulwar, and the Serpentreach holds, Ovdal Tûngr greatly benefited from the exchange of ideas from the rise and fall of the civilizations around them. This was most true when it came to trade policies. This administrative advantage combined with their long lives, led to the copper clans holding debts over most of the great houses across bulwar. Whenever the political tide turned against Ovdal Tûngr, they could leverage these debts to ensure their advantage. This changed, however, with the arrival of Jaher and his elven legions. To ensure the loyalty of his conquests, Jaher banished all dwarves from his realm and forgave all debts they owned. In response, Ovdal Tûngr sided itself with the resurgent Castanor led by the Sorcerer-King. When Jaher took arms against Castanor, he ordered a blockade of Ovdal Tûngr. "The Copper Enclosure" as it was called would last for over a century until the onset of the First Cinder War.

description.text: While copper makes for fantastic hull coating in the warm waters of the Divenhal, its heavy price prohibited its use in mass throughout the ancient world. This was not true for Ovdal Tûngr, however, sitting on their vast reserves of the metal mined from their mountain. Copper Bottoms as they are known among the humans were pivotal in the dwarven primacy along the Divenhal trade routes. These ships required less hull maintenance and lasted longer than their muscle encrusted competitors. And if the copper dwarves ever found themselves short on a trade investment, the sale of a few ships was enough to settle any debt.

description.text: The depths of Ovdal Tûngr were flooded long ago by unknown means. With Hul-Jorkad and its pumping equipment as one of the first victims of the Last Days, the dwarves of the reclamation lacked the knowhow to undertake the massive pumping effort required to reclaim the lower levels of the hold. In 1491, however, a visiting dwarven inventor by the name of Grun Strongbellow would propose a new hydraulic system that could drain even the deepest of mines. Soon the dwarves were not only delving the depths of their lost mines, but were also sending exploratory expeditions off the coast of Bulwar in copper diving helms.

description.text: The greatest gift Strongbellow left Ovdal Tûngr with was the design of a primitive steam engine to power his pumps. While the technology wouldn't exist for several more decades, once the steam engine was running, it wasn't long before dwarves figured out all sorts of steam powered oddities and trinkets. Only a century later would their full potential be discovered as a means to move the paddles of large ships. These "steamers" as they were called revolutionized water trade as ships could now more easily move upstream along the Suran to the ever expanding Jadd Empire and along the Alen to the burgeoning realms of Escann.

player_overview.avoid_if: Avoid if you dislike long-term saving and trade-right requirements, or cannot accept the forced expulsion of Goblins.
player_overview.how_it_plays: Secure Bahar and your allies first, then protect trade routes and build maritime commerce before saving the capital for steam and Sea Hold projects.
player_overview.overview: Ovdal Tûngr is a coastal hold governed by Copper Dwarf clans. Reclaim the area around the port, build a fleet and trade network, and cooperate with the neighboring human republic; invest the proceeds in the hold, drainage, and steam engineering. The Uthojdihr gain influence as the country revives, while the Strongbellow Society ultimately drives construction of a mobile fortress at sea. Long-term capital accumulation and trade-right arrangements set the pace, and the revival also involves the forced expulsion of Goblins.
player_overview.recommended_for: Players who enjoy naval trade, tall development, technological progress, and cooperative diplomacy.
signature_features: The hold's economy shifts from traditional mining toward drainage, undersea exploration, and a home at sea.
Relations with Crathánor, a fellow trading republic, affect routes and mission requirements.
Strongbellow engineering links steam, ironclads, and major capital investment into a long-term project.
player_overview.tagline: Restore a coastal hold through trade, then build the Dwarven home out at sea.

reasons: Naval trade directly sustains the hold and its major engineering projects.
The technology story runs continuously from undersea exploration to a fortress at sea.
Republican diplomacy and cooperation with Crathánor create different solo and multiplayer dynamics.
warnings: The Sea Hold requires enormous funds and production in a specified province.
In multiplayer, overlord arrangements or trade-right transfers can obstruct progress.
The revival includes Goblin expulsion; Sea Hold operations and DLC requirements were not tested in-game.

positive_indicators: Repairing the hold, ports, and maritime trade infrastructure.
Cooperation with the human republic and increased tolerance and population presence for the relevant groups.
Human oarsmen are described as hired; this is not treated as proven slavery.
values.rationale: The four-dimension weighted score is 52.25, rounded to 52. Repairing the hold and maritime infrastructure, hiring human oarsmen, and cross-cultural cooperation provide public benefit. The mission for province 527 explicitly removes all Goblin minorities and adds 25 devastation; a Bahar event removes its Goblin minorities if Goblin culture has not been accepted. These specific expulsions reduce dignity, personhood, and restraint. Goblin identity, republican government, trade, expansion, and colonization are not scored as inherently good or evil, and hired oarsmen are not recast as enslaved. Compared with the 110-country mirror, this scores below I12 Glass Lords (73) and is weighed against I14 Westroad (46), which combines development with ethnic removal, and H76 Gemradcurt (61), a commercial hegemon. Cross-cultural cooperation is real, but Goblin exclusion is explicit; hence Neutral 52. The Sea Gate Clan's rise is not equivalent to total autocracy. No reliable 20-point phase change in values was established; evidence is mixed, and in-game population consequences and multiplayer choices were not fully checked. Confidence is medium.
red_flags: The required mission for province 527 removes all Goblin minorities and causes devastation.
The Bahar governance event removes its Goblin minorities if Goblin culture has not been accepted.
Accepting Crathánor as a subject also involves local Goblin removal; this is not mandatory for every Ovdal Tûngr campaign.
